issues.legal_issue: A father’s liability arising from negligence in managing an institution is not an avyavaharika debt merely because it results from misfeasance.
material_facts: The father was a paid managing director of a bank.
A liability was imposed on him for negligence in the discharge of his duties, including the improper investment of the bank’s funds.
The sons challenged the sale of family property to satisfy that liability, but the record did not establish that the debt arose from conduct repugnant to good morals.
issues.conclusion: The liability was not avyavaharika, and the father’s debt was binding on the sons.
issues.legal_principle: Colebrooke’s translation of avyavaharika as a debt for a cause repugnant to good morals is the nearest approach to its meaning in the Smriti texts. The Court relied on Hem Raj alias Babu Lal v. Khem Chand for that meaning and Toshanpal Singh v. District Judge of Agra to distinguish criminal breach of trust from a civil liability for money received but not accounted for. Under section 43 of the Indian Evidence Act, the earlier payment order could not prove the truth of the facts stated in it; it could establish the existence of the order. Negligent performance by a paid managing director, in the circumstances, was not conduct repugnant to good morals.

predicates.sons_challenge_family_property_sale_for_: The sons challenged a sale of family property made to satisfy a debt imposed on their father.
predicates.father_received_remuneration_for_managem: The father received remuneration for managing an institution.
predicates.debt_arose_from_negligence_in_duties: The father’s liability arose from negligence in performing his management duties.
predicates.debt_shown_to_arise_from_immoral_or_ille: Evidence established that the father’s debt arose from an immoral or illegal purpose.

issues.definition: When sons challenge a family-property sale for a remunerated father’s negligent management debt, and the debt is not shown to arise from an immoral or illegal purpose, the debt binds the sons.

issues.legal_issue: Partition does not end a son’s liability for a father’s pre-partition debt that is not tainted with immorality or illegality.
material_facts: A payment order was made against the father before the partition suit was filed.
The family property was attached and sale proceedings had begun before the partition suit.
The debt was not shown to have been incurred for an immoral or illegal purpose.
No arrangement for payment of the father’s debt at partition was established.
issues.conclusion: The sons’ pious obligation continued after partition, and their shares remained liable to satisfy the father’s debt.
issues.legal_principle: The sons’ liability rests on their pious obligation, not solely on the father’s power to alienate their shares. Partition ends that power of alienation but does not discharge the sons’ liability for a father’s pre-partition debt that is not immoral or illegal, unless payment of the debt was provided for at partition. The Court relied on Panna Lal v. Mst. Naraini and Sudheshwar Mukherji v. Bhubneshwar Prasad Narain Singh, and applied the principles in Nanomi Babuasin v. Modun Mohan and related authorities on a creditor’s ability to proceed against the sons’ interests.

rule.if: execution_of_pre_partition_father_debt and debt_not_tainted_with_immorality_or_illegality and partition_after_decree and no_payment_arrangement_at_partition

predicates.execution_of_pre_partition_father_debt: A creditor sought in execution to recover a debt incurred by a father before partition.
predicates.debt_not_tainted_with_immorality_or_ille: The father’s debt was not tainted with immorality or illegality.
predicates.partition_after_decree: The family partition occurred after the decree against the father.
predicates.no_payment_arrangement_at_partition: No arrangement for paying the father’s debt was made when the family partitioned.

issues.definition: When execution concerns a father’s pre-partition debt that is not tainted with immorality or illegality, and partition follows the decree without a payment arrangement, the sons’ shares remain liable for the debt.

issues.legal_issue: Sons need not be separately impleaded in execution when their pious obligation for the father’s debt continues after partition and the sale is of the whole family estate.
material_facts: The decree and attachment preceded the suit for partition.
The property was attached and notice of sale was given before partition was sought.
The sale proceedings covered the whole property, and the sons did not notify the creditor or the authority conducting the sale of the partition suit.
The debt was not shown to be immoral or illegal.
issues.conclusion: The sons’ absence as named parties in the execution proceedings did not defeat the purchaser’s rights or require a separate suit, because the sons’ liability continued and they could challenge the sale by proving an immoral or illegal purpose for the debt.
issues.legal_principle: Where sons’ pious obligation continues, partition changes the mode of enjoyment but does not end the liability of their shares. After attachment and proper notice, a sale of the whole estate is not defeated merely because the sons were not named in the execution proceedings. The Court relied on Panna Lal v. Mst. Naraini, Sudheshwar Mukherji v. Bhubneshwar Prasad Narain Singh, and Nanomi Babuasin v. Modun Mohan. It distinguished Khiarajmal v. Daim, which concerned persons who were neither parties nor represented in the relevant proceedings and whose interests were not covered by the decree.

predicates.execution_against_father_for_non_immoral: A creditor pursued execution against a father for a debt not shown to be immoral or illegal.
predicates.attachment_and_sale_notice_precede_parti: The property was attached and notice of its sale was given before partition was sought.
predicates.whole_family_estate_is_sold: The execution sale covered the whole family estate rather than only the father’s separate interest.
predicates.sons_not_named_in_execution: The sons were not named as parties in the execution proceedings.

issues.definition: When execution for a non-immoral debt proceeds against a father, attachment and sale notice precede partition, and the whole family estate is sold, the sons’ omission as named parties does not defeat the sale.

issues.legal_issue: The extent of property conveyed at an execution sale is determined from the estate put up for sale, the sale authority’s intention, and what the purchaser intended to buy and paid for.
material_facts: The sale notice, proclamation, confirmation order, and sale certificate described the whole property rather than a fractional interest.
The purchaser bought and paid for the whole property.
The sale took place under the state revenue-recovery procedure using language corresponding to the civil-procedure description of a judgment debtor’s right, title, and interest.
issues.conclusion: The whole property, including the sons’ interests, passed to the auction purchaser.
issues.legal_principle: The words describing a defaulter’s right, title, and interest have the same connotation as the corresponding words in the civil procedure code in force when the revenue code was enacted. The interest conveyed is a question of fact determined from what was put up for sale, what the authority intended to sell, and what the purchaser intended to buy and paid for. The Court relied on Mulgund Co-operative Credit Society v. Shidlingappa Ishwarappa, Rai Babu Mahabir Prasad v. Markunda Nath Sahai, and Meenakshi Naidu v. Immudi Kanaka Rammaya Kounden, and distinguished Shambu Nath Pandey v. Golab Singh, where the documents showed that only the father’s interest was intended to pass.

rule.if: revenue_recovery_auction and sale_documents_describe_entire_property and purchaser_intended_to_buy_entire_property and purchaser_paid_for_entire_property

predicates.revenue_recovery_auction: The property was sold at an auction conducted to recover a debt through a public revenue-recovery process.
predicates.sale_documents_describe_entire_property: The notice, proclamation, confirmation, or certificate described the entire property as the subject of sale.
predicates.purchaser_intended_to_buy_entire_propert: The purchaser intended to buy the entire property rather than a fractional interest.
predicates.purchaser_paid_for_entire_property: The purchaser paid for the entire property.

issues.definition: When a revenue-recovery auction’s documents describe the entire property and the purchaser intended to buy and paid for all of it, the entire property passes to the purchaser.
